draft.title: Inclusion in sport
card: Inclusion means a sport is set up so that people of different backgrounds and abilities can take part and feel they belong. It goes further than letting people join.
Policies set the rules for a sport or club. A club can have a policy on anti-discrimination, on welcoming members, or on how its teams and facilities are used.

Clubs can include people in practical ways. They can adapt rules or equipment for people with disability, and offer programs that respect cultural and religious needs, such as clothing choices or prayer times.
Clubs can also work with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and use welcoming, respectful practices. They can offer gender-diverse people safe facilities and a place on a team.
draft.remember: Inclusion means changing how a sport is run so more people can take part and belong.

a.q: Which action by a club best shows inclusion?
opts: Adapting rules and gear so players with disability can join in
Allowing anyone to join but making no changes for them
Running one program at one time for all of its members
Letting players choose the team that suits them best
a.why: Inclusion means setting up the sport so people can take part and belong, so adapting rules and equipment is inclusion in action. Allowing people to join without any changes is the tempting option, but the card says inclusion goes further than letting people join.
a.clue: Inclusion goes further than letting people join.

b.q: Many players at Karim's netball club are Muslim, and some do not play because the uniform does not suit their beliefs. Which change would best include them?
opts: Offer uniform choices that respect their beliefs and needs
Tell them they are welcome to wear the current club uniform
Start a separate club that is held at a different ground
Let them watch games and help with scoring instead
b.why: Inclusion means changing the club so people can take part and belong. A uniform option respects cultural and religious needs and lets them play. Telling them they are welcome sounds friendly, but it changes nothing, so the barrier stays.
b.clue: Which option changes the club, not the player?
